articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 19, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 19, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, August 19, 2026
From private equity firm KKR picking up a minority stake in BookMyShow to Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath investing Rs 200 crore in hyperscale data centre operator Ctrls, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest news
PE firm KKR picks up minority stake in BookMyShow
Global private equity giant KKR has picked up a minority stake in digital ticketing platform BookMyShow for an undisclosed value.
A statement from KKR said the investment will support BookMyShow's next phase of growth as it aims to scale its live entertainment business with the goal of bringing global artists to Indian audiences, and deepen its full-stack offering across India.
Funding news
Nikhil Kamath invests Rs 200 Cr in Ctrls’ Rs 250 Cr fund raise
Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath has invested Rs 200 crore in CtrlS, the India based hyperscale data centre operator, alongside a Rs 50 crore investment by entrepreneur Sreeram Reddy Vanga.
CtrlS will use this capital to support its infrastructure expansion and capacity build-out to meet growing enterprise and hyperscaler demand across India, particularly as AI, cloud, and digital workloads accelerate.
Butterfly Learnings raises Rs 65 Cr funding
Butterfly Learnings, an Indian paediatric behavioural healthcare platform focused on children with neurodevelopmental conditions, has raised Rs 65 crore in a pre-Series B funding round led by Inflexor Ventures, a venture capital firm that backs early-stage technology companies.
Existing investors Enzia Ventures, Insitor Impact Asia Fund and IIMA Ventures also participated in the round.
First Coffee raises $1.3M to expand specialty coffee chain
Specialty coffee chain First Coffee has raised $1.3 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Japanese venture capital firm DG Daiwa Ventures, with participation from BEENEXT and other investors. The company said the funding will support store expansion, team building, marketing and product development. It has now raised $2.5 million in total.
Founded in 2024, First Coffee operates a grab-and-go model and currently has more than 25 outlets across Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. The company plans to expand beyond North India and enter Tier 2 markets as it targets growth in India's rapidly expanding specialty coffee sector.
AlgoFET raises Rs 15 Cr to expand autonomous drone infrastructure
Bengaluru-based drone infrastructure startup AlgoFET has raised Rs 15 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Piper Serica. Founded in 2023, the company develops autonomous ground infrastructure that enables drones to dock, recharge and relaunch with minimal human intervention, supporting continuous and unattended operations.
AlgoFET said the funding will be used to accelerate product development, expand manufacturing, strengthen proprietary technology and scale deployments across defence, enterprise and international markets. The company has deployed more than 2,000 units, has a pipeline of over 4,000 units and works with drone manufacturers and the Indian Army. It also operates a 12,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in Bengaluru.
Neuromod Aqua raises pre-seed funding to scale modular wastewater treatment
Neuromod Aqua has raised a pre-seed funding round from Sportskeeda founder Porush Jain to develop a factory-manufactured platform for decentralised sewage and effluent treatment. The company is building modular wastewater treatment plants using established technologies such as MBBR, MBR and SBR, while standardising design, manufacturing, installation and maintenance.
The funding will support manufacturing, product development, commercial deployments and the expansion of engineering and service capabilities. Neuromod plans to generate recurring revenue through maintenance, operations, compliance support and remote monitoring. Over the next year, it aims to launch its manufacturing facility and complete initial deployments in the Delhi NCR region.
Other news
AWS to open Builder Loft in Hyderabad
AWS will launch a Builder Loft in Hyderabad as part of its global expansion of the community-focused initiative, alongside new locations in Berlin and São Paulo. The permanent space will offer free workshops, networking events, pitch sessions, co-working areas, content creation facilities and event hosting for developers, students and technology professionals.
The Hyderabad centre will focus on AI and cloud-native technologies, providing developers with opportunities to build technical skills, collaborate with peers and access hands-on learning. The expansion follows the launch of the first AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco and reflects the company's focus on supporting India's growing developer community.
Amazon expands rail logistics network on Western Dedicated Freight Corridor
Amazon India has expanded its operations on Indian Railways' Western Dedicated Freight Corridor in partnership with the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India. The company has become the first e-commerce platform to operate on the Joint Parcel Product-Rapid Cargo Service train on the corridor, with daily rail movements linking its northern and western logistics network.
The route will connect Delhi, Ahmedabad and Surat, with onward links to Pune, Mumbai and Goa, shifting more shipments from road to rail ahead of the festive season. Amazon began using Indian Railways for parcel movement in 2019 and now operates more than 140 trains across 130 intercity routes serving over 100 cities.
Garuda Aerospace partners with Australian drone platform company TAS
IPO-bound Garuda Aerospace has signed an agreement with Australia's Timed Automation Solutions to collaborate on autonomous drone technologies. The partnership will combine Garuda's drone manufacturing and services capabilities with TAS's expertise in autonomous aerial operations, including drone-in-a-box systems, fleet management, AI-assisted image analysis and enterprise software integration.
The companies will explore opportunities in product distribution, joint technology development and domestic and international projects across sectors such as agriculture, infrastructure inspection and remote operations. The collaboration will also assess pilot deployments in Australia and New Zealand as Garuda expands its international presence.
World Economic Forum names Cropin a global innovator
The World Economic Forum has named agri-tech company Cropin a global innovator, recognising its work in applying artificial intelligence to agriculture. The recognition follows Cropin's earlier selection as a Technology Pioneer and will see the company contribute to the Forum's Centre for Nature and Climate.
Cropin operates in 103 countries and uses AI to help address challenges related to climate change, food security and agricultural productivity. The company said it has digitised more than 30 million acres of farmland, built intelligence covering over 1 billion acres and supported more than 7 million farmers.
Only 9% of Indian finance certification candidates feel prepared for an AI-driven job market
Only 9% of Indian finance certification candidates believe they have the skills needed to compete in an AI-driven job market, compared with 67% of graduates in a global CFA Institute survey, according to SSEI's Finance Talent Pulse 2026.
The survey found that 56% of Indian respondents believe AI and automation are making it harder to secure their preferred roles, while only 7% regularly use AI tools for financial analysis or modelling.
Practical experience emerged as the biggest concern, with 42% identifying it as their main skills gap and 42% reporting that they had never used AI in real financial work. The study surveyed 133 India-based CFA, FRM and CA candidates and compared the findings with a global survey of 9,000 graduates across 11 countries.
Avanade appoints Achal Kataria as India Managing Director and CEO
Avanade has appointed Achal Kataria as Managing Director and CEO for India, effective immediately. Kataria will lead the company's business strategy and operations in the country, with a focus on expanding its market presence and helping organisations scale digital and AI transformation initiatives.
He joins Avanade from Cognizant, where he led the company's India business. He has more than 30 years of experience across technology services, enterprise transformation and global operations. The appointment reflects Avanade's focus on India as a growth market, driven by increasing adoption of cloud technologies and enterprise AI.
Roamiyo launches travel app combining trip planning and collaboration tools
Roamiyo has launched a travel app that combines itinerary planning, group coordination and on-trip management in a single platform. The app offers three core features including personalised itinerary planning, Group Mode for shared trip coordination and Trip Mode for managing schedules while travelling.
Users can create customised itineraries, collaborate through shared plans and group chats, split expenses, store travel documents and access tools such as navigation, currency conversion, language translation and weather updates. Following a private beta involving more than 2,000 users, Roamiyo plans to focus on user growth and product development.
MJ Digital Services launches Cashlo app for small retailers
MJ Digital Services has launched the Cashlo app, a digital business platform designed to help shopkeepers offer financial and utility services while creating additional income opportunities.
The platform enables merchants to provide services including UPI-based cash withdrawals, digital payments, mobile and DTH recharges, electricity, water and gas bill payments, FASTag services and other BBPS transactions.
Cashlo also offers access to personal, business and working-capital loan services through participating merchants. Additional features include Quick Khata for digital credit record management and tools covering accounting, GST and ITR requirements.
1% Club launches AI CFO
Finance creator and entrepreneur Sharan Hegde’s 1% Club has launched AI CFO, an AI-powered financial tool designed to provide personalised guidance and help users make better money decisions. The launch marks the company’s transition from a financial education platform towards a technology-led personal finance ecosystem. AI CFO is designed to understand an individual’s financial context and offer relevant guidance based on their needs.
It uses information such as cash flow, net worth, portfolio and holdings, along with 1% Club’s research, without requiring users to manually enter their financial details. The platform also offers portfolio reviews across eight parameters, including returns, fund quality, benchmark performance, allocation, concentration, overlap, cost and tax position.
Blue Machines AI launches Floe
Enterprise conversational AI platform Blue Machines AI has launched Floe, a proprietary context-aware language detection model designed for multilingual conversations. The model helps AI agents identify not only the language being used by customers but also whether they actually intend to switch languages during a conversation. Built around India’s multilingual communication patterns, Floe currently supports English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Bengali, Odia and Punjabi.
The technology distinguishes between the presence of a language and a user’s actual language preference. It analyses words, parts of speech, sentence structure, short utterances and previous conversational context before deciding whether an AI agent should continue responding in the current language or initiate a switch.
Snowflake introduces dynamic AI model routing
Snowflake has announced dynamic model routing within Cortex AI Gateway and its flagship AI products, along with expanded access to leading open models. The company said the new capabilities are aimed at helping enterprises reduce unnecessary AI spending and improve “intelligence efficiency” by optimising the use of compute, models, data and context. Cortex AI Gateway provides a unified foundation for governing agent connections, routing requests and managing AI consumption.
Dynamic model routing automatically selects a model based on the required balance of quality and cost. Lower-complexity or repetitive tasks can be directed to more efficient models, while tasks requiring deeper reasoning are routed to frontier models. The capability is also integrated with Snowflake CoCo and Snowflake CoWork and is available to third-party AI agents.
CRED launches Circle by CRED
Fintech platform CRED has launched Circle by CRED, a new app designed to give members access to experienced individuals for personalised conversations and decision-making support. Through Circle, members can have one-on-one interactions with “Residents” who bring expertise across careers, money, wellness and relationships. Select members can access more than 100 Residents during the beta phase.
The service builds on CRED’s 1.7-crore community and is positioned as a way to provide members with fresh perspectives and practical guidance. Residents can act as thought partners, helping members interpret situations, recognise patterns and make decisions. Members can connect through text, audio or video between 6 pm and 10 pm, seven days a week. Pricing starts at Rs 25 per minute.
Hexaware launches Zero Vulnerability cybersecurity offering
Hexaware Technologies has announced Zero Vulnerability, a cybersecurity offering combining its expertise in cybersecurity, engineering, AI and remediation operations. The offering covers different IT environments, including custom applications, SaaS and PaaS platforms, third-party software and operating systems. Its remediation operating platform supports the complete lifecycle from ingestion and validation to prioritisation, routing, fixing, verification and closure.
The platform is designed to work alongside existing security and workflow tools rather than requiring enterprises to replace them. Hexaware’s evaluation across four detection lanes on production codebases consolidated 334 findings, of which 14 were ultimately verified as genuine vulnerabilities. A developer-validated review of 262 findings also identified an authentication-bypass weakness that had been missed by pattern-based rules.
Agent B Studio launches Visual AI platform
Agent B Studio has launched a Visual AI platform designed to bring the design workflow into a single connected system. Powered by a multimodal AI orchestration engine, the platform enables architects, interior designers, furniture brands and real estate developers to design, visualise, specify and deliver projects through one workflow. Unlike conventional AI image generators, Agent B Studio generates spatially accurate, photorealistic renders using real floor plans and dimensions.
Its tools include Layout to Render, Quick Generate, Smart Project, Photo Edit and Bella, an AI assistant. The platform also allows brands to integrate product catalogues directly into design workflows, connecting visualisation with commerce. Agent B Studio said it crossed 5,000 designer signups within 10 weeks of launch, with professionals adopting it as an end-to-end workflow solution.
Hostinger expands AI Builder into agentic platform
Hostinger is expanding beyond AI-generated websites with AI Builder, an agentic platform designed to help users build, run and grow online businesses. The platform combines AI-led creation and visual controls with backend infrastructure, ecommerce, embedded AI and marketing capabilities. It is designed to allow AI to establish and operate systems behind a project rather than simply generate an initial website.
Hostinger said the shift is particularly relevant for India’s small and mid-sized businesses seeking greater operational efficiency. AI Builder can help businesses create inventory trackers, order logs, customer databases and internal portals alongside websites and online stores. The company said projects outside traditional website categories have risen from less than 4% a year ago to nearly one in five today, including SaaS products, internal tools and learning platforms.
Embark launches GCC cost calculator
Embark, a platform focused on helping companies establish and expand Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India, has launched a web-based GCC Calculator. The tool provides companies with an instant estimate of the fully loaded cost of setting up and operating a GCC in India. It can also be used by companies already running GCCs to benchmark and validate their existing cost structures.
Users enter details including team size, roles and headquarters location, after which the calculator generates a cost model covering compensation, benefits, real estate, technology, infrastructure, compliance and one-time setup expenses. It also compares the cost of the same team with expenses in the company’s home market. Features include multi-geography, sector and currency support, CapEx amortisation, multiple locations and roles, and instant self-serve calculations.
Neo4j highlights growth among AI-native startups
Graph intelligence platform Neo4j has highlighted growing adoption among AI-native startups in India across sectors including fintech, enterprise AI, legaltech, healthtech, compliance, edtech and sports technology. These companies are part of Neo4j’s global Startup Program, which provides AI-native founders with cloud credits, technical enablement and go-to-market resources to help scale AI systems. The programme was launched as part of Neo4j’s $100 million investment in graph-powered AI.
The company said the initiative addresses challenges faced by enterprises attempting to move generative AI projects into production. According to the source document, MIT research shows that 95% of enterprise GenAI pilots fail to reach production, with lack of contextual understanding cited as a key challenge. Neo4j positions graph technology as a way to provide that contextual layer.

articles.title: Cette start-up chinoise pose le premier étage de sa fusée dès le deuxième vol
articles.text:
LandSpace a récupéré sur la terre ferme le booster de Zhuque-3 après avoir placé un satellite en orbite. Une prouesse encore réservée à trois entreprises privées dans le monde.
Deux vols, et déjà un atterrissage. Le 19 août, la start-up chinoise LandSpace a réussi à faire revenir verticalement le premier étage de sa fusée Zhuque-3, six minutes après son décollage de Dongfeng. Dans le même temps, le second étage plaçait le satellite Honghu-03 sur l’orbite prévue. C’est la première fois que la Chine récupère à terre, sur des pieds déployables, un étage de lanceur orbital.
Un premier échec corrigé en huit mois
Lors du vol inaugural de décembre 2025, Zhuque-3 avait bien atteint l’orbite, mais son booster s’était écrasé et avait explosé près de la zone d’atterrissage après une combustion anormale durant la phase finale. Pour cette deuxième tentative, la start-up a notamment revu la propulsion d’atterrissage, le contrôle du retour et les protections thermiques. Le premier étage a pu enchaîner changement d’attitude, freinage propulsé, descente aérodynamique contrôlée et ultime rallumage avant de se poser debout.
L’exploit propulse LandSpace aux côtés de SpaceX et Blue Origin, les deux seules autres entreprises privées à avoir posé un booster de classe orbitale. La Chine avait certes récupéré un Long March 10B en juillet, mais au moyen d’un filet installé en mer. Selon Reuters, LandSpace vise désormais jusqu’à 20 vols par étage et prévoit de faire revoler un booster récupéré dans les six mois.
Côté européen, le contraste pique. Ariane 6 n’est pas réutilisable et Themis, le démonstrateur européen d’étage réutilisable piloté par l’ESA, n’avait encore réalisé fin juillet qu’une répétition générale avec de l’azote liquide. Son premier petit bond vertical reste à venir.

articles.title: ChatGPT activa Computer History, la función que rastrea tus clicks y todo lo que escribes en el PC
articles.text:
Hacer que tu trabajo sea más fácil y rápido tendría un costo: que ChatGPT sepa todo lo que haces en tu PC y lo pueda memorizar. Esta función fue presentada por OpenAI, llamada Computer History y le dará a la IA la capacidad de recordar tareas, documentos y hábitos para facilitar el trabajo diario desde el computador.
El objetivo de esta herramienta es hacer que las consultas y automatizaciones sean cada vez más personalizadas y eficientes, ya que el chatbot tendrá la capacidad de entender el uso que se hacen de ciertas aplicaciones y páginas web.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué es Computer History y cómo funciona
Computer History es una función recientemente presentada en la aplicación de escritorio de ChatGPT para macOS. Su objetivo es registrar la actividad del usuario en el ordenador, permitiendo que la inteligencia artificial adquiera una memoria contextual de lo que se realiza en diferentes aplicaciones y páginas web seleccionadas.
A diferencia del historial convencional del navegador, Computer History abarca todo el entorno del PC. La función va recopilando información sobre los programas en uso, los documentos abiertos, los textos escritos y los cambios entre aplicaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Todo este flujo de datos se traduce en una línea temporal y en resúmenes textuales que pueden ser consultados tanto por ChatGPT como por Codex, el modelo orientado a la automatización.
La activación de Computer History es completamente opcional. El usuario decide en todo momento qué aplicaciones y sitios web incluir en el registro. La función no graba imágenes, ni audios, ni videos, ni tampoco toma capturas de pantalla. Además, excluye cualquier actividad realizada en modo incógnito o privado del navegador.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué permite hacer Computer History
La posibilidad de que ChatGPT recuerde la actividad del usuario abre nuevas formas de interacción con la inteligencia artificial. El sistema puede, por ejemplo, responder preguntas como “¿dónde guardé ese archivo con determinado contenido?” o “¿en qué estaba trabajando antes de la pausa?”.
También es capaz de sugerir automatizaciones para tareas que se repiten a menudo, o ayudar a retomar actividades que se dejaron a medias.
El funcionamiento de Computer History se basa en la creación de “eventos de interacción”. Estos eventos incluyen acciones como clics, escritura de textos, uso de atajos de teclado y cambios entre aplicaciones. Periódicamente, los eventos se agrupan en resúmenes en formato de texto y archivos de memoria que se almacenan localmente en el Mac del usuario.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta memoria permite que ChatGPT responda de manera más precisa, conociendo el contexto sin que el usuario deba explicarlo en cada consulta. La IA puede identificar rápidamente en qué documento se trabajó la última vez, si fue compartido por Slack, o qué páginas se consultaron durante la jornada.
Cómo será la privacidad y el control por parte del usuario
Uno de los puntos centrales de Computer History es el control sobre la privacidad. La función está desactivada por defecto y solo se activa si el usuario lo permite explícitamente desde el menú de ajustes de la aplicación de ChatGPT en macOS. Desde ahí, se pueden seleccionar las aplicaciones y webs que serán monitoreadas, así como revisar o eliminar bloques de historial cuando se desee.
PUBLICIDAD
Los archivos de eventos se almacenan en el Mac durante 48 horas antes de ser procesados por los servidores de OpenAI. Tras el procesamiento, la compañía asegura que los datos temporales no se conservan, a menos que exista una obligación legal. Los resúmenes textuales, por su parte, permanecen en el equipo hasta que el usuario decida borrarlos manualmente.
Estos resúmenes se guardan en formato Markdown y no están cifrados, por lo que cualquier programa con acceso a la misma cuenta de usuario podría leerlos.
PUBLICIDAD
OpenAI advierte también de la posibilidad de que, al dar acceso a la actividad del ordenador, existan riesgos adicionales de que un sitio web o programa malicioso intente manipular al asistente mediante instrucciones ocultas. Esta advertencia figura en la documentación técnica oficial y subraya la importancia de revisar los permisos y la configuración antes de activar la función.
Por ahora, Computer History solo está disponible en la aplicación de escritorio de ChatGPT para macOS y el acceso está limitado a usuarios de pago, quienes deben contar con una suscripción a ChatGPT Pro, Business o Enterprise. Los usuarios de la versión gratuita de ChatGPT no tienen acceso a esta función.

articles.title: A fantastical journey unfolds in gorgeous Wildwood trailer
articles.text:
In June, we highlighted a behind-the-scenes featurette on the making of Wildwood, director Travis Knight’s forthcoming stop-motion animated fantasy film. Laika Studios released an extended teaser in May, which racked up over 90 million views. And now we’ve got the gorgeous full trailer, set to a haunting cover of Avicii’s “Wake Me Up.”
The film is an adaptation of the 2011 novel by Colin Meloy—frontman of indie folk-rock band The Decemberists—and his wife, illustrator Carson Ellis. Meloy and Ellis live in Portland, Oregon, near Forest Park, where they often hike the trails. In Wildwood, they transformed that local landmark into a magical hidden world filled with talking animals and lurking threats, only accessible to people of The Wood—and select Outsider “half-breeds.”
Twelve-year-old Prue McKee discovers the forest while out walking with her baby brother, Mac. A murder of crows swoops down and carries him away, and Prue discovers the Wilderness while hunting for him. Her schoolmate, Curtis Mehlberg, follows her, and both are able to enter that magical world. Fantastical adventures ensue as the pair encounter a mysterious woman, Alexandra, who has lost her son, along with coyotes, bandits, and some pretty big secrets.

articles.title: Memória RAM chinesa quebra barreira e pode ser bom sinal para crise • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Memória RAM chinesa quebra barreira e pode ser bom sinal para crise
Fabricante chinesa alcançou uma marca notável com um kit DDR5 em teste de overclocking. O avanço aproxima a China das gigantes globais do segmento de memórias.
Se a solução para a atual crise das memórias virá da China, é difícil dizer. Mas não dá para negar que a indústria do país está engajada com o segmento. Prova disso é que a CXMT conseguiu fazer um kit de memórias DDR5 alcançar a marca de 9.000 MT/s na transferência de dados em um teste de overclocking, o que a aproxima das gigantes do setor: Micron, SK Hynix e Samsung.
Convém esclarecer que MT/s significa megatransfers por segundo. Esse parâmetro é particularmente útil para memórias RAM porque representa a taxa efetiva de transferências de dados desses componentes.
1 MT/s é o mesmo que um milhão de transferências por segundo. Logo, 9.000 MT/s correspondem a 9 bilhões de transferências por segundo.
O teste de overclocking em questão foi conduzido pela Colorful, empresa chinesa que produz placas-mãe, placas de vídeo e outros componentes para PCs.
Com o uso de uma placa-mãe Colorful iGame X870E VULCAN W OC trabalhando com um processador AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, o kit Colorful iGame Shadow II com 48 GB de memória DDR5 conseguiu ultrapassar a tal marca de 9.000 MT/s operando a 4.507 MHz — foram 9.014 MT/s, para ser exato.
Os resultados foram divulgados na rede social chinesa Weibo e encontrados pelo TechPowerUp. Embora o kit de memórias leve a marca Colorful, a fabricação de seus chips foi feita “internamente”, ou seja, por uma empresa chinesa: justamente a CXMT.
É verdade que testes similares feitos com kits de memória dos mencionados rivais já alcançaram marcas ainda mais impressionantes, que superam 13.000 MT/s em overclocking. Mesmo assim, a taxa de 9.000 MT/s é tido como um avanço notável para uma empresa que ainda está se desenvolvendo no segmento de memórias RAM.
A CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies) é a maior fabricante de chips de memória da China. A empresa surgiu em 2016 e, nos últimos meses, atraiu uma crescente atenção no mercado global.
Isso porque, diante da dificuldade das referências do setor — relembrando, Micron, SK Hynix e Samsung — de darem conta da demanda atual por memórias, os módulos da CXMT são vistos como alternativas em potencial.
Mas ainda há desconfiança sobre a capacidade tecnológica da CXMT. Apesar disso, testes como o realizado pela Colorful sugerem que a fabricante chinesa tem conseguido reduzir a distância de qualidade em relação a seus rivais.

articles.title: Pew survey: 52% of Americans now more concerned than excited about AI
articles.text:
The takeaway: Artificial intelligence is seemingly everywhere these days, but public attitudes toward the technology are changing. For some, the excitement surrounding AI has given way to outright concern, but will the industry take notice and take steps to ease worry?
A recent report from the Pew Research Center reveals that more than half of US adults – 52%, to be exact – are "more concerned than excited" about the increased use of artificial intelligence in daily life. That is up from just 37% who answered the same way in 2021 when Pew first asked the question.
Only nine percent of those polled in 2026 said they were more excited than concerned over what AI brings to the table. Back in 2021, nearly one in five – 18% – said they were more excited than concerned. Roughly a third of the US adult population – 37% – said they were equally concerned and excited about AI.
Job loss is a leading worry among concerned citizens. In the latest survey, which was conducted June 22-28 of this year, 71% of Americans said they believe AI will lead to fewer jobs for humans over the next 20 years. When the same question was asked two years ago, only 64% of Americans thought AI would lead to less jobs in the workforce.
Only five percent of respondents were optimistic on the topic and believe AI will lead to more jobs for humans in the next two decades.
Also interesting is the fact that age no longer seems to play a role in this question, as worry about job loss now shows up across all polled demographics. Younger people, however, have their own concerns with AI.
As recent studies have shown, younger adults tend to view AI negatively overall and feel it could hamper creativity and their ability to foster relationships. In a September 2025 Pew study, 61% of young adults said AI could harm their ability to think creatively and 43% felt it would make solving problems more difficult.

articles.title: Google Pixel 11 Review: The one to buy if you need an upgrade
articles.text:
The Pros
- Solid hardware
- Capable camera
- Intelligence that's actually helpful
The Cons
- Tensor G6 is better, but not enough
- Battery can't keep up with heavy use
- More expensive
This year, Google is continuing its trend of subtle refinements with its Pixel line. The new Pixel 11 sports a handful of new features and enhancements, but at first glance doesn’t seem that different from its predecessor.
Moreover, the base Pixel model remains in a somewhat awkward spot, squeezed between a more budget-friendly ‘A’ model — currently the Pixel 10a and presumably the 11a that’s likely to come next year — and the more capable Pro models. (Stay tuned for a full review of the Pixel 11 Pro in the coming days!)
But it’s not just an internal squeeze. The Pixel line (and most smartphones coming out this year) also have to contend with ongoing component shortages, such as RAM, thanks to AI companies and other factors.
The result? A base Pixel model that costs a little more than before without doing much to change the formula. For the Pixel fans out there, the Pixel 11 is more of the same great phone you’ve come to know and love, with a few new features and not much else.
What’s actually new
So, what’s actually new this year? Well, there are a few things. Starting with the hardware, there are some external changes including some awesome new colours (I’m a huge fan of the Hibiscus shade pictured in this review) and Google significantly cut down the thickness of the camera bump compared to the Pixel 10. (The Pro models retain their larger camera bump, however.) It’s also a bit lighter than the Pixel 10, which is always welcome.
The only other noticeable external change is the layout of the camera bar, which trades the Pixel 10’s dual-tone metal and glass approach for a uniform black glass, and a new LED flash that looks like HiLight, but isn’t — HiLight is exclusive to the Pro models.

There are some internal hardware changes as well, including a slightly larger battery (4,985mAh to the 10’s 4,970mAh), more storage (the Pixel 11 starts at 256GB instead of 128GB), and the new Tensor G6 chip and Titan M3 security coprocessor.
Camera hardware also remains relatively unchanged, with the Pixel 11 sporting a 48MP main camera with an 85-degree field of view (the Pixel 10 was 82-degree FOV), a 13MP ultrawide camera, and a 10.8MP telephoto camera offering 5x optical zoom. Aside from the slight FOV change, the main sensor is also larger, which should improve performance in low-light scenarios. The Tensor G6 sports an upgraded imaging signal processor (ISP) that should help improve capture speeds, with Google touting 4.5 times faster Night Sight processing.
There are a handful of new software features as well, like Magic Capture and Camera Looks, and a suite of tools aimed at content creators like grid lines optimized for social media and a built-in teleprompter feature. But we’ll get into these in more depth below.
Fly like a G6?
Google touted some major upgrades to the Tensor chip this year, noting that the upgraded CPU offers 25 per cent faster web browsing and 15 per cent quicker app launches. Tensor G6 also features 50 per cent more compute for running local AI like Gemini Nano — Google says it’s up to 3.5 times faster and uses 3.5 times less energy.
In my time with the Pixel 11 so far, it absolutely feels snappy, though I can’t say it’s noticeably faster than the Pixel 10 Pro I was using before. However, one area I did notice improvement was thermals. I find the Pixel 11 doesn’t get as warm as the 10 Pro during intensive tasks like gaming.
I haven’t benchmarked the Pixel 11 yet, mostly because benchmarking tools like Geekbench aren’t available for the device yet, but once they are, I’ll add the results to this review.
Still, Pixel phones have never been benchmark champs and yet typically offer really solid performance in real-world use. During my testing time, I had no noticeable slowdowns or other performance issues.
Unfortunately, the Pixel 11 isn’t much better than its predecessors when it comes to battery life. With my typical usage, including messaging and emailing, streaming music, browsing social media, watching YouTube, and occasionally playing some games, it was able to make it from around 7 a.m. to around 11 p.m. There usually wasn’t enough to stretch into a second day if I forgot to charge overnight, however.
But on heavy-use days, like when I go into the office and use the Pixel 11 for hotspotting, the battery drains much more quickly. Obviously, hotspotting is a more intensive task, but on those days I was hunting for a charger by 4 p.m.
On the whole, I’d say performance is improved compared to the 10 series, but not by significant margins. Anyone coming from an older Pixel phone may appreciate these improvements more.
Capable cameras
Next up, let’s chat cameras. With the Pixel 10, I felt like the base model was able to produce results that were good enough despite having worse camera hardware than the Pro models.
The same holds true with the Pixel 11, which is able to pump out some fantastic shots. The better hardware available on the Pro models can definitely help in more challenging scenarios, like lowlight or zoom shots, but Google’s computational photography is able to squeeze the most even out of lesser sensors.
In head-to-head comparisons, there’s not a ton of difference between the Pixel 11 and Pixel 10 main sensors. Both produce similar results with good colours and details.
Things get a little more interesting with the telephoto camera. At the base bx optical zoom, results are very similar, although I will note the slight differences in colour. The Pixel 11 does a better job bringing out the green hues in the bandshell compared to the Pixel 10, but otherwise quality is about the same.
Google boasted that the Pixel 11 sports 30x ‘Super Res’ zoom, which uses the telephoto camera mixed with other techniques like AI to improve the quality loss from going beyond the optical zoom’s upper limits. Most of the time, I’d recommend that people stick to the optical zoom, or maybe go up to 10x Super Res — beyond that point, things start to fall apart. That said, the Pixel 11 does a pretty good job of keeping the lettering on the bandshell and other details clear with Super Res Zoom. I’d argue it comes pretty close to the 10 Pro’s 30x zoom in terms of overall quality.
One of the other big additions this year is Camera Looks, which offers four “professional-grade film presets” and the option to create your own. This totally rips off Apple’s Photographic Styles feature that launched on the iPhone 16 series. Based on my testing, I don’t notice much difference between the styles. I also found them to be annoying to change on the fly, so I just stuck with the ‘Original’ style for my photos.
Other new camera features include Magic Capture, which offers a combination video and photography mode. Users can switch the camera into Magic Capture mode and tap the shutter button to start a video-like capture. In the background, the Pixel 11 analyzes the frames and automatically pulls out the best shots for you. On paper, it sounds really neat, but I haven’t had enough time using this feature yet to say if it works as well as promised.
There’s also the aforementioned creator suite with storyboarding features, social media grid lines, audio visualizer, and teleprompter features. I’m not really one to make TikToks or other video content, but these features look great for those who are into doing that.
Overall, the Pixel 11 camera carries on the tradition of being pretty good. It’s not the best camera on a phone, but it’s quite capable and should be sufficient for the majority of users. While I appreciate the extra hardware capabilities of the Pro cameras for work purposes, the Pixel 11 makes a fantastic everyday camera.
Other software goodies
Finally, Google added a ton of new software goodies to the Pixel 11, some of which will likely make their way to older Pixels (if they haven’t already). Google’s Magic Cue system got an upgrade and is now called ‘Proactive Assistance.’ I still don’t find it as useful as Google thinks it is, but I’m definitely seeing it more often on the Pixel 11 than I did on the Pixel 10 or 10 Pro. I’ve already used it a few times to add events to my calendar, which is quite handy.
Proactive Assistance can also show up in new ways, such as location-based tips appearing in Pixel’s ‘At a Glance’ widget on the home screen. However, this capability is still in preview, and it hasn’t shown up yet for me.
Elsewhere, Google’s Live Translate got an upgrade that allows for real-time speech-to-speech translation, enabling the phone to automatically dub videos into your language.
And for speech-to-text enthusiasts, the Pixel 11 sports Rambler, which is better able to strip out filler words so you can speak more naturally when using voice input.
While the above changes are all welcome, I’m not sure any of these are compelling enough to drive a phone purchase. They feel more like nice bonuses that make an upgrade you’re already doing feel better, rather than must-have capabilities that will move phones.
Worth the upgrade?
On the whole, the Pixel 11 is a really good phone. It gets a lot right, has a solid camera system, and a bunch of smart features that make the phone feel more helpful than competitors. At the same time, Google’s hardware remains a bit behind the curve, and price increases don’t help matters either.
The Pixel 11 retails for $1,249 for the 256GB model in Canada, or $1,419 for the 512GB. Last year’s Pixel 10, on the other hand, cost $1,099 for the 128GB model and $1,229 for the 256GB. So the price increase isn’t huge if you compare the 256GB options, but the lack of a cheaper 128GB model definitely hurts here.
While it’s generally a bad year to upgrade your tech thanks to all of the rising prices, I do think that those with older Pixel models like the 7 or 8 would see enough benefits to justify an upgrade. And if you’re trying to choose between the Pixel 11 and 11 Pro, I’d say stick with the 11 unless you’re a real camera snob.
For what it’s worth, this is the Pixel phone I would buy for myself if I were in the market for an upgrade.
The Google Pixel 11 is available for pre-order now, and launches on Aug. 20, 2026.

articles.title: Best Buy cuts $168 off the 8TB Seagate IronWolf HDD, but it's still cheaper at Newegg
articles.text:
You can save $168 on this 8TB Seagate IronWolf NAS drive at Best Buy, but I'd shop elsewhere for an ever better deal
The CMR hard drive suits NAS systems, RAID arrays and multi-user environments
Adding a lot of dependable capacity to a NAS device isn't cheap, but shopping around can net you major savings. The 8TB Seagate IronWolf is currently $350 (was $518) at Best Buy. But I wouldn't buy it there. Newegg has the exact same drive for $330, saving you a further $20.
IronWolf is purpose-built for NAS use, with 24/7 operation and multi-drive environments in mind. This 8TB model uses CMR recording technology, spins at 7200 RPM and has a 256MB cache, making it a solid choice for expanding a home NAS, small-business server or RAID array.
Seagate rates it for workloads of 180TB per year and 1 million hours MTBF. AgileArray provides RAID optimization and dual-plane balancing. Rotational vibration sensors are designed to help maintain consistent performance when several drives are operating together.
The Seagate IronWolf ST8000VN004 provides 8TB of CMR capacity, 7200 RPM performance, 256MB cache and SATA 6.0Gb/s connectivity, with a 180TB/year workload rating and rotational vibration sensors.
This is the exact same drive, and while it's a solid $167.66 off the list price at Best Buy, it's still $20 more than you can pick it up for at Newegg.
Why we recommend it
In his 4-star review of the 8TB NAS drive, our expert Mark said: "IronWolf drives feature CMR technology and AgileArray firmware, ensuring smooth RAID performance, reduced vibration, and efficient power management. The 180TB per year workload rating, the RV sensors, the three-year warranty, and the bundled Rescue Data Recovery Services have all persisted as defining features of the consumer tier."
The 7200 RPM spindle speed and 256MB cache and SATA 6.0Gb/s interface makes this a performance-focused mechanical drive rather than simply somewhere to dump 8TB of rarely accessed files.
For more options, take a look at our roundups of the best desktop and laptop hard drives and best NAS hard drives.
Price context & historical value
Best Buy is currently selling the 8TB Seagate IronWolf for $349.99, which is a massive $167.66 reduction off the usual $517.65 asking price.
While that looks like a brilliant deal on paper, the identical drive is $329.99 at Newegg, a saving of $187.66 which means you're paying about $41.25 per terabyte.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the 8TB Seagate IronWolf NAS drive if...
You need a high-capacity drive to cope with the demands of an always-on NAS. The combination of 8TB capacity, CMR recording and 7200 RPM makes this a strong option for backups, media libraries, and shared files.
It's particularly well suited to multi-bay and RAID setups. AgileArray is designed to optimize RAID performance, while the built-in rotational vibration sensors help the drive maintain consistent operation when it's surrounded by other spinning hard drives.
❌ Skip the 8TB Seagate IronWolf NAS drive if...
You only need additional storage for an ordinary desktop PC. Although you can use an IronWolf as a conventional SATA hard drive, much of what you're paying for is specifically intended for NAS environments, including 24/7 operation, RAID optimization and vibration management.
I'd also look elsewhere if silence and low power consumption are priorities. A 7200 RPM mechanical drive is designed with performance in mind and won't offer the near-silent operation of an SSD.
The Catch: What to know before you buy
NAS manufacturers maintain compatibility lists for their enclosures, and checking your system supports this exact ST8000VN004 model can save headaches later, particularly if your NAS is a little old.
It's also important to remember that RAID isn't a substitute for a separate backup. The 8TB IronWolf can provide plenty of capacity and is designed for RAID environments, but drive redundancy doesn't protect you from accidental deletion, malware, theft or failure of the NAS itself.
Also consider
The larger 12TB IronWolf model combines 7200 RPM performance with a 256MB cache, up to 210MB/s read and write speeds, IronWolf Health Management, and included Data Recovery Services.

articles.title: Graphwise aims to become the semantic layer for AI agents after securing major investment from Oakley Capital - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Graphwise aims to become the semantic layer for AI agents after securing major investment from Oakley Capital
Graph database startup Graphwise said today it has secured a significant, though unspecified, investment from the European venture capital firm Oakley Capital as it looks to beef up its go-to-market strategy and expand globally.
It will also use the funds to pursue strategic acquisitions, it said. Oakley has acquired a majority stake in the Bulgarian startup from a consortium of investors that include Integral Capital Group, PortoLion Capital Partners, Carpathian Partners and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. It did not disclose the size of the deal.
Graphwise is the creator and developer of an open-source graph database called GraphDB, which makes it possible to store contextual data alongside business records, such as information about which specific store a sale took place in. This isn’t possible with traditional Structured Query Language databases, because their architecture doesn’t allow for these connections to be discovered easily.
According to Graphwise, the GraphDB platform is designed to address the gap between raw data and the need for actionable knowledge that can enhance the capabilities of large language models. So instead of treating content and data as separate concerns, it creates an intelligent fabric that connects them together.
To do this, GraphDB is based on a knowledge graph that provides a dynamic, interconnected view of enterprise content and how it relates to the database records. It works by encoding relationships, hierarchies and metadata in such a way that AI models can derive user’s intent, suggest related topics and support scenario-based recommendations.
For instance, documents will be auto-tagged with both user-specified taxonomies and content-derived semantics. The key element here is GraphDB’s so-called “semantic layer,” which is uniquely able to manage both structured data and unstructured content, while maintaining consistent semantic metadata that ties this information together.
Graphwise believes that this architecture is just what’s needed to support autonomous artificial intelligence agents that can perform work on behalf of humans without supervision. AI agents are powered by large language models that are extremely good at processing natural language.
However, they’re also infamous for their factual inconsistencies, known as “hallucinations,” and an inability to explain their reasoning. Graphwise changes this, grounding LLMs in a reliable and governed layer of verifiable enterprise facts that agents can retrieve information from and reason across.
To support AI agents, GraphDB uses a technique called GraphRAG, which helps them retrieve the precise, contextual information the underlying model needs to respond to a prompt. It’s an especially useful capability for regulated and data-intensive industries such as financial services, healthcare and life sciences, where strict data governance, auditability and compliance are essential requirements.
Another advantage GraphDB provides to AI agents is cost benefits. Because it feeds models very specific, contextual information instead of just drowning them in masses of unstructured data, agents can dramatically reduce the amount of data they need to process, which means much lower token consumption.
These are the reasons why Oakley Capital decided to take a majority stake in Graphwise. It’s going to work closely with Graphwise President Antanas Kiryakov to enhance its commercial capabilities and expand its footprint into international markets. The startup has already made good progress in that regard and counts over 200 “blue-chip customers” and an organic annual recurring revenue growth rate of more than 30%.
Oakley Capital founder and Managing Partner Peter Dubens said trusted, well-governed data is more important than ever because every enterprise desperately wants to make the most of AI agents, wherever they can. “Graphwise has built an exceptional platform to solve that challenge and has already demonstrated impressive growth,” he said.
